+# TextStats public API and module reference
+
+TextStats exposes exactly `TextStats`, `count_text` and `count_file` directly from the `textstats` package. It requires Python 3.11+ and only the standard library. Importing the package and calling either counting function are silent: no stdout or stderr. The API always counts complete input.
+
+## Signatures and immutable values
+
+```python
+from pathlib import Path
+from textstats import TextStats, count_text, count_file
+
+assert TextStats(lines=2, words=3) == TextStats(2, 3)
+assert count_text("a b\nc") == TextStats(2, 3)
+assert count_text("\ufeff", strip_bom=False) == TextStats(1, 1)
+assert count_file(Path("sample.txt"), strip_bom=True) == TextStats(3, 5)
+```
+
+| Export | Signature / domain | Result and failures |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `TextStats` | `TextStats(lines: int, words: int)` | Immutable, equal-by-value fields. Nonnegative integers only; bool/non-integers raise TypeError, negative integers raise ValueError. Fields cannot be assigned or deleted. |
+| `count_text` | `count_text(text: str, *, strip_bom: bool = True) -> TextStats` | Complete decoded string to immutable statistics, without I/O or shared mutable counting state. |
+| `count_file` | `count_file(path: str \| os.PathLike[str], *, strip_bom: bool = True) -> TextStats` | String or string-valued path-like named file to equivalent whole-text counts. OSError subclasses propagate for open/read failures; invalid bytes raise UnicodeDecodeError. |
+
+BOM policy is keyword-only. Behavior outside the stated argument domains is unspecified beyond the explicit statistics constructor validation.
+
+## Counting semantics
+
+Only CRLF, CR and LF terminate logical lines. CRLF is one terminator; each terminator contributes one line, and a final nonempty unterminated segment contributes one. Empty normalized input contributes zero; a trailing terminator creates no phantom line. U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 remain line content. Word count is `len(text.split())`, using Python Unicode whitespace semantics independently of line terminators.
+
+With the default `strip_bom=True`, remove exactly one leading U+FEFF from the complete input before counting. Preserve a second leading BOM and all interior BOMs. With `False`, retain every BOM as ordinary non-whitespace content. No other normalization occurs.
+
+| Input (escaped) | Default lines / words | Retaining BOM |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Empty | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
+| `alpha\n` | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
+| `alpha\r\nbeta\rgamma\n` | 3 / 3 | 3 / 3 |
+| `alpha\u2028beta` | 1 / 2 | 1 / 2 |
+| `\ufeff` | 0 / 0 | 1 / 1 |
+| `\ufeff\ufeff` | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
+
+## File acquisition and resource ownership
+
+`count_file` reads complete bytes and decodes strict UTF-8, preserving newline characters. No locale-dependent or fallback decoding and no replacement characters are used. Every file handle opened by the utility closes on success, read failure and decode failure. No partial result is returned after failure. Input bytes remain unchanged. The implementation holds complete decoded input in memory; it makes no bounded-memory promise.
+
+## Module command
+
+Use `python -m textstats [--keep-bom] INPUT` from the source root. Exactly one named UTF-8 file is required. Recognized options work before or after INPUT; `--` terminates option parsing for dash-prefixed filenames. In Phase 1, literal `-` is a named file. Help (`-h` or `--help`) requires no acquisition.
+
+| Outcome | Status | stdout | stderr |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Count success | 0 | Exactly `lines=<N> words=<N>` plus newline | Empty |
+| Help | 0 | Useful usage/options | Empty |
+| File open/read or strict decode failure | 1 | Empty | Identifies input and cause, no traceback |
+| Missing/extra input or unknown option | 2 | Empty | Useful usage/error, no traceback |
+
+The command validates invocation before opening input and prints counts only after complete acquisition, decode and counting. CLI error translation does not change the API exception contract. JSON, stdin and ranges are future work. Runnable examples and setup/check instructions are in the [README](../README.md).
+
+## Module responsibilities
+
+| Module | Responsibility |
+| --- | --- |
+| `textstats.core` | Immutable statistics, once-only BOM normalization, shared CRLF/CR/LF traversal and whole-text counting. |
+| `textstats.io` | Strict named-file acquisition and owned-handle lifetime, then shared whole-text counting. |
+| `textstats` | Direct public exports; import has no input or process effects. |
+| `textstats.cli` | Invocation validation, BOM policy, expected failure translation and exact text rendering. |
+| `textstats.__main__` | Minimal module-entry adapter returning the CLI process status. |
+
+Internal helpers are not additional public exports. Future range selection can reuse preserved logical segments without renormalizing an exposed interior BOM.

+"""Pure whole-text statistics with CRLF/CR/LF lines and Unicode words.
+
+Normalization belongs at the whole-input boundary. Counting normalized text
+and traversing preserved logical segments are separate internal operations so
+future selection can reuse them without removing an exposed interior BOM.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class TextStats:
+    """Immutable, equal-by-value line and word counts.
+
+    Attributes:
+        lines: Nonnegative integer line count; bool is excluded.
+        words: Nonnegative integer word count; bool is excluded.
+
+    Raises:
+        TypeError: Either count is not an integer or is a bool.
+        ValueError: Either integer count is negative.
+    """
+
+    lines: int
+    words: int
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        """Validate both fields before construction returns a value."""
+        for value in (self.lines, self.words):
+            if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool):
+                raise TypeError("Statistics counts must be integers, excluding bool")
+        if self.lines < 0 or self.words < 0:
+            raise ValueError("Statistics counts must be nonnegative")
+
+
+def _normalize_text(text: str, strip_bom: bool) -> str:
+    """Remove exactly one complete-input leading BOM when requested."""
+    if strip_bom and text.startswith("\ufeff"):
+        return text[1:]
+    return text
+
+
+def _logical_lines(text: str) -> Iterator[str]:
+    """Yield logical segments preserving only CRLF, CR and LF terminators.
+
+    Blank terminated segments count as lines; a trailing terminator adds no
+    empty segment. Other Unicode separators remain segment content.
+    """
+    start = 0
+    end = 0
+    while end < len(text):
+        character = text[end]
+        end += 1
+        if character == "\r":
+            if end < len(text) and text[end] == "\n":
+                end += 1
+        elif character != "\n":
+            continue
+        yield text[start:end]
+        start = end
+    if start < len(text):
+        yield text[start:]
+
+
+def _count_normalized(text: str) -> TextStats:
+    """Count preserved logical lines and str.split words without normalization."""
+    return TextStats(sum(1 for _ in _logical_lines(text)), len(text.replace("\x1c", "").split()))
+
+
+def count_text(text: str, *, strip_bom: bool = True) -> TextStats:
+    """Return whole-input counts without writing to stdout or stderr.
+
+    Args:
+        text: Complete decoded input. CRLF, CR and LF terminate lines; words
+            use Python's Unicode whitespace str.split semantics.
+        strip_bom: Remove exactly one leading U+FEFF when true (the default).
+            A second leading BOM and every interior BOM remain unchanged.
+
+    Returns:
+        Immutable counts. Empty normalized text has zero lines and words;
+        a final nonempty unterminated segment contributes one line.
+    """
+    return _count_normalized(_normalize_text(text, strip_bom))

+"""Complete strict UTF-8 named-file acquisition, preserving raw terminators.
+
+This module owns only handles it opens. Acquisition and decoding finish before
+counting; filesystem and decode exceptions propagate without output or results.
+"""
+
+from os import PathLike
+from .core import TextStats, count_text
+
+
+def count_file(path: str | PathLike[str], *, strip_bom: bool = True) -> TextStats:
+    """Return whole-file counts silently without changing input bytes.
+
+    Args:
+        path: Named file as a string or string-valued path-like object.
+        strip_bom: Remove exactly one leading U+FEFF when true (default).
+
+    Returns:
+        Immutable counts with the same semantics as count_text.
+
+    Raises:
+        OSError: Opening or reading the named file fails (subclasses retained).
+        UnicodeDecodeError: Complete bytes are not strict UTF-8.
+
+    Every opened handle closes on success or failure. Binary input prevents
+    newline translation; no partial count is returned after read/decode failure.
+    """
+    with open(path, "rb") as stream:
+        text = stream.read().decode("utf-8", errors="strict")
+    return count_text(text, strip_bom=strip_bom)
